description: ignorePaths replaces config:recommended's list rather than merging with it, so the list is restated: it is the one Renovate 45.1.0's :ignoreModulesAndTests preset gives (lib/config/presets/internal/default.preset.ts, lines 306-317), without **/test/** and **/tests/**. Test folders are read, so that a dependency a test uses, such as a test module's go.mod, gets updates like any other. A repository that must keep one ignored names it in its own renovate.json, as divbast/pisati does for test/acceptance.

logLevelRemap.description: An update Renovate cannot date, such as a rebuilt digest on a registry that gives no timestamp, is not held, by choice: minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour is timestamp-optional. Renovate still warns, on every run, that it went ahead without a timestamp, and each warning is listed under Repository Problems on the Dependency Dashboard, where it reads as something to fix. Info keeps the line in the run's log and off the dashboard.
logLevelRemap.matchMessage: /^Some (release|upgrade)\(s\) did not have a releaseTimestamp, but as we're running with minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-optional, proceeding/

customManagers.description: The BuildKit image docker/setup-buildx-action runs, pinned by a driver-opts line, where no default manager reads it.
The SBOM scanner image BuildKit runs for --attest type=sbom, pinned as its generator argument, where no default manager reads it.
The registry image a workflow starts to rehearse a publish. Only the line after a '# renovate: registry' marker is read, so no other registry image in a workflow is touched.

The mise release jdx/mise-action installs, pinned as MISE_VERSION in a workflow env block under a '# renovate:' marker. mise tags its releases v2026.11.7; the action takes the bare form, which is what the README shows, so the v is stripped.

packageRules.description: Subject prefix for the local toolchain: mise.toml, composer-pinned tools, Go modules and npm-pinned tools such as a CSS build's compiler. Kernel style, 'subsystem: short description', because these are commits on main like any other.
Subject prefix for the github-actions manager's upgrades: the action pins and the reusable-workflow refs, divbast/ci's among them.

Subject prefix for the build tools the shared regex managers above pin in workflows. A manager cannot carry commitMessagePrefix itself, and the github-actions rule does not reach a custom.regex upgrade.
Subject prefix for a repository's image build inputs, wherever a Containerfile or Dockerfile appears. Kernel style, 'subsystem: short description', because these are commits on main like any other.

ci's pin check refuses a repository whose divbast/ci refs name more than one SHA, and a repository calls several reusable workflows on several lines. Every ref therefore has to move in one commit, so they share one group and one PR.
A new major of divbast/ci is minted by any commit there that carries a Breaking-change: trailer, so a person approves it from the Dependency Dashboard. Minor and patch releases keep automerging.

jq tags releases as jq-1.8.2. mise strips that prefix from aqua's registry entry; Renovate does not read the aqua registry, so without this every candidate version is discarded as unparseable and no PR is ever raised.

trivy is looked up on Docker Hub, not GitHub. The aquasecurity org has an IP allow list, and GitHub enforces it on API reads by an App installed on an organisation, as divbast-renovate is, so every github-tags or github-releases lookup is refused and the 403 surfaces only as no-result. mise still installs from the release download, which the allow list does not cover. aquasec/trivy is pushed by the same GoReleaser run that publishes those binaries, tagged with the same bare version. Docker versioning keeps latest, canary and the older per-architecture tags such as 0.71.2-amd64 out of the candidates.

The go line in go.mod is a language version, not a library. Bump, not widen, because go-mod-directive versioning reads go 1.27.0 as ^1.27.0 and would otherwise never propose anything. Raising it can enable newer vet checks, which ride on the go line and can fail a build that passed before, so a person approves it from the Dependency Dashboard.

github.com/divbast/ci reaches each repository through a replace to a local .ci/ checkout that the workflow refs pin, so the go.mod version is a placeholder. The github-actions digest on those refs is the one dependency that moves it, and a gomod PR would only churn the placeholder.

Every release of outside code waits 3 days before Renovate proposes it, by minimumReleaseAge above, so a bad or pulled release has time to be found before a divbast repository takes it. divbast's own releases, its actions and reusable workflows, Go modules and images, are built and tested in the divbast organisation, so they never wait. This rule is the preset's last, so no rule above it holds them again. Security updates are not held either: Renovate opens them at once.
